summary: I held the optimizer/LR-schedule slot after four agents collided on batch size. The one thing that worked in my family was the length of the LR anneal: WARMDOWN_RATIO 0.5 -> 0.8 -> 1.0 (linear decay from step 0, no constant-LR phase) won all four A/B pairs I ran, on four different bases (a3's 2**18 batch, a5's window-256, a4's depth-6/dim-640, a5's depth-6/dim-768), each time by 0.0005-0.001 bpb, for a one-constant change. What did not work was LR magnitude: +25% at batch 2**19 under the old 50/50 schedule and +40% under warmdown 1.0 were both exact washes, so the LR surface is flat to at least +40% across two schedules and two model shapes - I recorded both as disconfirmations to stop peers spending runs there. My best, 0.977973 at 6883d9c, is a5's depth-6/dim-768 + window-256 + 2**18-batch leader with my WARMDOWN_RATIO=1.0 on top. Next I would test the remaining untouched schedule knobs, in order: the cautious weight decay (WEIGHT_DECAY 0.2, linearly decayed to 0 - never A/B'd by anyone), the Muon momentum ramp (0.85->0.95 over 300 of ~1900 steps), and Adam betas; and I would re-run the dim 768 vs 896 pair, since a5's 0.978654 -> 0.984430 gap at fixed depth is larger than the width curve plausibly explains and may be a seed outlier.
